entries.note: A very minor CME see to the NW in LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and fully covered by the data gap in STEREO A COR2. It is possible that this CME is an outflow following the 2026-11-06T16:15Z CME. No clear source for this CME has been found.

Wide CME visible to the NW in GOES CCOR-1 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. The CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery in real-time due to a data gap starting at 2026-11-06T13:38Z. The likely source is a filament eruption that starts to lift off in STEREO A EUV 304 imagery, around N35W140, starting at 2026-11-06T13:15Z. The filament can also be seen lifting off beyond the west limb in GOES SUVI 304 imagery.  Moving/opening field lines are also visible in SDO AIA 171 in ISWA, SDO AIA 193, and GOES SUVI 284 imagery.

CME visible to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME may also be faintly visible to the NNE in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The start of the CME may be faintly visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2  at the time of the analysis, but was not visible in SOHO LASCO C3 in real time due to a downlink data gap. The source is an eruption just on or beyond the NE limb as seen in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284 imagery seen as opening field lines starting at 2026-11-06T06:16Z.

Narrow CME visible to the west in STEREO A COR2. The CME is not clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery is not available due to a downlink data gap. The potential source is an eruption seen near the west limb in STEREO A EUV 195/304 located around N20W160 starting around 2026-11-06T03:15Z. The eruption can be seen as an ejecta of material in STEREO A EUV 304. Moving field lines and post-eruption arcades are also visible in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery.

Narrow CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source may possibly be a minor eruption starting around 2026-11-06T00:22Z in as best seen in SDO AIA 193, with moving field lines seen around S15E70.

CME seen to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME is also faintly visible to the east in STEREO A COR2 after a data gap from 2026-11-05T14:35Z to 2026-11-06T01:38Z. The potential source location may be a minor eruption seen near the SE limb in GOES SUVI 304 imagery starting around 2026-11-05T19:28Z located near S15E75. Moving/opening field lines are also best seen in SDO AIA 171/193 imagery.

CME first seen in white light imagery to the E in GOES CCOR-1 starting at 2026-11-05T20:00Z. In real time, this CME is covered by data gaps in SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is like related to an M3.5 class flare from AR 14566 (S08E35) which peaked at 2026-11-05T18:33Z. The flare is best seen in SDO AIA 131. Some post-eruptive dimming can also be seen in SDO AIA 193. Due to the source location being in close proximity to a coronal hole, some deflection is likely.
CME faintly visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The CME is not clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1 or STEREO A COR2 imagery. There is no clear source for this CME seen in available EUV imagery.

CME faintly visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source is unclear, but may be a small eruption seen near the northeast limb in GOES SUVI 304 as an ejecta of material starting around 2026-11-05T03:24Z.

Faint CME first seen to the NW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-11-04T02:48Z. This CME fades before exiting the field-of-view in SOHO LASCO C2, and is therefore not visible in GOES CCOR-1 or SOHO LASCO C3. This CME and source are also obscured by a data gap in STEREO A COR2 from 2026-11-03T18:23Z to 2026-11-04T04:23Z. The source of this event is field line movement seen beyond the NW limb beginning at approx. 2026-11-04T02:00Z as seen in SOD AIA 171.

Wide, slow CME observed to the E in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap beginning at 2026-11-03T18:36Z. This CME is very slow to erupt, speeding up well after its first observation in SOHO LASCO C2. The source is observed in GOES SUVI 171/195/284 starting loosely around 2026-11-03T08:00Z as wide, slow field line movement lasting several hours on/near the E limb, and source may be slightly far-sided.

Slow developing CME first seen to the NE by SOHO LASCO C2, also observed in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not observed in STEREO A COR due to a data gap in real-time starting at 2026-11-01T19:38Z. The source of this event is an eruption from beyond the NE limb seen in GOES SUVI 284/304 beginning at approx. 2026-11-01T18:14Z as filament ejecta and very wide, slow field line movement. An initial faint CME at 2026-11-01T18:36Z (LASCO C2) measuring plane-of-sky ~164 km/s is observed prior to this brighter emerging front.

CME first seen to the West in SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-11-01T19:00Z. The CME is also visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The CME may be faintly visible to the east in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source of this event is a filament eruption seen centered at approx. N15W15. Filament destabilization began at approx. 2026-11-01T16:43Z, with liftoff beginning at approx. 2026-11-01T17:54Z as seen in SDO AIA, STEREO A EUVI and GOES SUVI 304. Post eruptive arcades and field line movement are also visible in SDO AIA 193, GOES SUVI 284 and STEREO A EUVI 195.

Diffuse CME first seen to the SE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-11-01T00:00Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is a small filament eruption seen centered at approx. S15E65 beginning at approx. 2026-10-31T23:25Z as seen in SDO AIA 304. Post eruptive arcades and field line movement is also visible in SDO AIA 171/193. This eruption is in close proximity to a coronal hole, potentially resulting in some deflection.
